To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
viral hepatitis has an impact on the serum levels of lipids, lipoproteins, apo-A, apo-B and lipoprotein ( a ) in the patients of liver diseases.

1) the serum levels of apo-A were significantly reduced in the groups of acute viral hepatitis and in fulminant hepate failure, 2) serum apo-B level was significantly low in the CAHe and cirrhosis group, 3) the low-density lipoproteins level was significantly high in the CAHe group, 4) the serum high-density lipoproteions level was significantly low (p = 2) in all groups except cirrhosis group and
The low-density lipopro-tein value was high in CAH group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of viral hepatitis on the lipid/lipoprotein status in different forms of viral hepatitis.
the impact of viral hepatitis on the lipid/lipoprotein metabolism in different forms of viral hepatitis.
the effects of different types of viral infections on the serum lipid/lipoprotein status in patients with liver diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is an association of hepatitis with low-density lipoproteins, whereas high-density lipoproteintions are reduced.
the changes in lipids/lipoproteins were not specific to the viral etiology of hepatitis, and that the severity of the disease was more closely related to the changes.
viral hepatitis is associated with a significant decrease in high-density lipoproteins, Apo-A and lipoprotein (A) levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
viral hepatitis, irrespective of its etiology, has a profound impact on the lipoprotein profile of the patient.
viral hepatitis is associated with significant changes in lipid/lipoprotein profile and apolipoprotein status in the serum.
the lipid/lipoprotein changes are related to the degree of liver injury and the type of liver disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a significant decrease in the high-density lipoproteins and Apo-A levels in patients with viral hepatitis.

the serum levels of Apo-A, Apo-B and lipoprotein (A) are significantly low in the patients suffering from acute viral hepatitis and chronic liver disease, whereas the level of low-density lipoproteins is high in chronic liver disease.
the lipoprotein status is affected by liver disease and not the etiological agent.
